item.title: Alaska Senate Race: Doubts About Democrats Are Republicans’ Best Asset
item.description: Democrat Mary Peltola has many things breaking her way in her bid to unseat Republican Senator Dan S. Sullivan in Alaska. But Sullivan has one big thing working for him. Whether that’s enough will likely determine whether he wins reelection — while also offering clues about the fate of other red-state Republican senators this year.
item.dc:creator: Ronald Brownstein

item.title: AfD Victory: Germany Is In a Very Dark Place and Time Is Running Out
item.description: The far-right Alternative for Germany’s dramatic election win in the eastern state of Saxony-Anhalt on Sunday is a watershed in the country’s postwar history. In a nation known in the modern era for stability, Germans in this small federal region have embraced populist, nationalist ideas in large numbers.
item.dc:creator: Chris Bryant

item.title: Bayeux Tapestry Exhibit Gives Clues About the UK's Future
item.description: Not since the treasures of the boy pharaoh Tutankhamun arrived in London over 50 years ago has there been such excitement over a blockbuster exhibition. The Bayeux Tapestry commemorating Duke William of Normandy’s victory over King Harold’s Anglo-Saxons at Hastings in 1066 will go on show at the British Museum this week. Around 100,000 tickets were snapped up in minutes. The Times of London calls it “the loan of the millennium.”
item.dc:creator: Martin Ivens

item.title: Switzerland Capital Plan for UBS Is Complex, Costly And Bad
item.description: Switzerland is searching for a better insurance policy against any failure of its last global bank, UBS Group AG. The latest proposal from lawmakers to make a financial crisis less likely to crash the economy is meant to protect taxpayers from any future bailout while keeping the lender competitive. But the plan is complex, costly and probably not even workable.
item.dc:creator: Paul J. Davies

item.title: Leasehold Reform: London's £431,000 Apartments Are Devalued by Stigma
item.description: Britons are souring on apartments. That’s a particular problem for London, where flats overwhelmingly account for new-home sales and construction has already slowed to a crawl, leaving housing supply at a fraction of government-set targets. Cratering demand presents a challenge to policy makers — as well as an opportunity for buyers willing to do their homework in a market sector that people are shunning.
item.dc:creator: Matthew Brooker

item.title: China’s Luxury Slowdown Leaves Fashion Brands Reliant on US Spending
item.description: A year ago, shoppers in Shanghai visiting The Louis, a massive Louis Vuitton emporium shaped like an ocean liner, were stocking up on pricey luggage, raising hopes that China’s luxury market was finally rebounding.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Felsted and Juliana Liu

item.description: In commodity markets, certain truths can be taken as self-evident.
